author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Two powerful earthquakes, magnitude 7.5 and 6.6, struck Panama, damaging buildings and forcing thousands onto the streets. Thousands rushed out of buildings, shopping malls and schools as the quake shook the country on Friday. The tremors were felt as far away as Colombia and Costa Rica.

The epicentre was in rural Herrera province, in central Panama. More than a hundred aftershocks have continued throughout Friday, including one measuring magnitude 6.6. Authorities reported no casualties by late Friday.

The earthquake also triggered tsunami warnings along the Pacific coast, from Panama to Peru and as far as Chile and Hawaii. At the Panama Canal, authorities activated emergency protocols, but shipping has continued uninterrupted.

Earthquakes this powerful are relatively rare in Panama, and with aftershocks continuing, people remain on edge.

Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump says he has spoken with Russian President Vladimir Putin about increasing diesel supplies to the global market. He posted that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons, then 500,000 in November and 1 million after, then 3 million. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the deal, calling it “an investment in war”.

Al Jazeera’s Manuel Rapalo, reporting from Washington, DC, says the deal could be significant, with fuel prices soaring before the midterms. But it is unclear how quickly shipments will arrive, how much will go to the US, and whether Russia can meet the commitments given its refining limits. 

Trump signed sanctions last month targeting Russia’s oil revenue, so the deal appears a striking reversal, drawing criticism mostly from Democrats.

Glenn Carle, a US national security specialist and former CIA officer, says the deal is largely hollow. He says US refineries are already near full capacity, Russian refining has been badly hit
title: US-Russia diesel deal would likely help Russia more than the US: Analysis

The Saudi-led coalition says it is carrying out a wide-ranging operation targeting the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah. It says it has destroyed 136 Houthi military targets and is giving round-the-clock air support to the Yemeni government army and forces loyal to it.

Air strikes hit Sanaa, which is under Houthi control, and there were reports of a loud explosion in the southern port city of Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based. 

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Sanaa, says he heard a loud explosion there shortly before his report. In the past 24 hours, he says, the capital has seen strikes at Sanaa International Airport, two factories, and at least four telecommunications sites. Mount Attan was hit by ten air strikes.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
New York Police Department footage shows the scene after a shooting by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.

Twenty-eight-year-old Oscar Belal was in a car when agents who were trying to arrest him opened fire seven times. His five-year-old son was in the car.

Demonstrators took to the streets afterwards. New York officials, including the state’s governor and the city’s mayor, condemned the shooting. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said: “ICE operates with impunity, and they sow chaos and terror across our country. That they have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save.”

The Department of Homeland Security defended the agents’ actions, saying Belal had attempted to run them over.

Data from TRAC Immigration shows that of more than 65,000 people in ICE detention in mid-July, more than 70 percent had no criminal conviction, and just four percent were convicted of violent crimes.
